purpose: Authoritative source registry for the 69-food evidence audit. This registry separates food composition, digestive physiology, clinical context and plant-specific feeding evidence; none of these categories may be silently substituted for another.

sources.publisher: Rural Development Administration / National Institute of Crop Science
sources.title: National Standard Food Composition Database 10.4
sources.reuse: Korea Open Government License Type 1 (attribution) applies to the annually updated database; verify attribution on publication.
supports: food-code and nutrient-value provenance after exact food/part/preparation reconciliation
does_not_support: plant identity when the food record lacks sufficient taxonomic resolution

sources.title: Important Factors in Chelonian Nutrition
sources.taxon_scope: Chelonia; includes practical tortoise nutrition context
does_not_support: individual plant safety verdict without plant-specific evidence

sources.title: Herbivorous reptiles and body mass: effects on food intake, digesta retention, digestibility and gut capacity, and a comparison with mammals
sources.sample_context: 23 tortoises in the added experiment, body mass range 0.5-180 kg
supports: digestibility and gut-capacity context in herbivorous tortoises
does_not_support: captive diet percentages for a specific plant

sources.title: Macroscopic, microscopic, and immunofluorescent characterization of the Greek tortoise (Testudo graeca graeca) oropharyngeal floor with concern to its feed adaptation as a herbivorous land reptile

guardrails: Food-composition data are descriptive and must not determine a tortoise feeding verdict.
A review or physiology study cannot be promoted to plant-specific evidence unless the plant and relevant outcome are directly studied.
Testudo graeca graeca evidence is not exact-subspecies evidence for Testudo graeca ibera.
Every future RDA mapping must retain the exact food code, Korean/English food name, edible part, preparation state, source/version and observation date.
When RDA and USDA both exist, preserve both provenance streams rather than overwriting one with the other.
